issues.description: Method SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery: The problem statement (UML and textual description) specifies a 4-parameter signature (supplierName: String, ingredientName: String, price: int, quantity: int). The template's example usage in Main.java and the solution implementation define acceptSupplyDelivery with a 3-parameter signature (ingredientName: String, price: int, quantity: int). This discrepancy between the documented API and the provided code/tests makes it unclear which signature students should implement and can lead to incorrect method signatures that fail to compile or not match tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter list consistent across all artifacts. Preferred minimal fix: update the problem statement (UML and textual description) to declare acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and remove the supplierName parameter from descriptions and diagrams so they match the template and solution. Alternative: if tracking a supplier is required pedagogically, change the solution and template calls to acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and update implementations and examples accordingly.

issues.description: The method for registering supply deliveries is described differently across artifacts. In the problem statement (UML and textual description) the method is specified as acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) — i.e., four parameters including a supplier name. In the template usage (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java) and in the solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java) the method is implemented and called as acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) — a three-parameter signature without a supplier argument. Students cannot reliably map the documented API to the provided code/usage because the parameter count and meaning differ, causing confusion about the expected parameters and their order.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent across documentation and code. Two valid choices: (A) Update the code and template calls to implement the four-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and update all call sites (e.g., Main.java) to pass a supplierName as the first argument; or (B) Update the problem statement (UML and textual description) to specify the three-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and adjust the UML method signature accordingly. Ensure the chosen parameter order and names are explicitly documented and that Main.java examples and the solution implementation match that chosen signature.
